messages:
Marta: FYI eu2 is seeing a big NVMe backlog right now, GPU attaches getting queued or falling back to network volumes. Noticed at ~02:55 UTC.
Diego: Metrics: avgqu-sz on nvme0-3 ~18, await ~30ms, util ~99%. p99 attach latency jumped to ~300ms.
Diego: iostat sample:
```nDevice:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm  %util
nvme1n1         900   2800  72000  224000   76.0    18.2   30.1   0.28  99.3
```
Lex: Scheduler shows ~40 pending GPU attaches, 12 failed and were routed to remote volumes (adds ~150ms median and big egress).
Marta: Any idea if this is janitor churn, batch writes, or firmware?
infra-bot: janitor-run: deep-scan sweep started on pool eu2-scratch at 02:50 UTC per policy window.
scheduler-bot: batch-wave: large model-rollout began at 02:52 UTC targeting eu2.
Diego: Correlating logs now 11 looks like overlap: janitor deep-scan + batch writes hitting hot stripes.
Lex: Short-term: recommend pausing the batch wave and throttling janitor for the region. Also prefer-local-affinity in attach logic so jobs avoid scarred nodes.
Marta: Agreed. Diego, can you estimate cost impact from remote fallbacks?
Diego: From samples: remote-attach egress + storage ops increased cost ~ $1200 over 30m for that rollout. Roughly +$0.012/token equivalent for high-throughput runs.
Marta: Ouch. Ops-oncall, can you pause batch deployments to eu2 for 20m?
ops-oncall: Pausing now, posting in #eng-oncall.
Lex: I'll push a temporary janitor rate cap to canaries:
``nkubectl patch cm janitor-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_concurrent_scans":"2","scan_delay_ms":"100"}}'
```
Lex: Will canary to 3 hosts then roll.
Diego: Also enabling attach-local-affinity flag on the scheduler:
``nsed -i 's/attach_local_affinity=false/attach_local_affinity=true/' /etc/scheduler/conf.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/scheduler -n infra
```
Marta: Add an alert for avgqu-sz > 10 and p99_attach > 200ms. We should get paged sooner.
infra-bot: Alert rule created: nvme_avgqu_gt_10_eu2, nvme_p99_attach_gt_200ms. PD notified.
Lex: If throttling doesn't help in 10m, plan B is to reschedule janitor to off-peak (00:00-02:00) and backfill with incremental scrubs. That reduces immediate IO but increases backlog risk.
Diego: Long-term ideas: smarter scrub scheduling that is stripe-aware and avoids nodes with high attach traffic; add a janitor-eviction-window when GPUs are provisioning.
Marta: Also log this cost delta per rollout so product/sales can be alerted; we shouldn't surprise customers with unexpected cost events.
ops-oncall: Batch wave hold in place. Monitoring p99 attach and avgqu.
Lex: Patch applied to canaries, avgqu-sz on canaries dropped from 18 -> 7 within 80s. Rolling to remaining canaries now.
Diego: Early telemetry looks better: attach p99 down to ~180ms on mitigated hosts. Overall pending attaches falling.
Marta: Good. Keep the hold until p99 < 150ms for 5 consecutive mins. Follow-up: postmortem and a new scheduler policy to avoid scrub+deploy overlap.
ops-oncall: Acknowledged. Will create incident ticket and schedule postmortem.
Marta: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
